name: Pretomanid
route_note: Oral tablet once daily, only in combination with bedaquiline and linezolid (with or without moxifloxacin).
targets: Mycolic acid synthesis and respiration (via reactive nitrogen species)
originator: PathoGenesis Corporation; developed by the TB Alliance
owner: TB Alliance (licensed to Viatris and others)

discovery.by: PathoGenesis Corporation (C. Kendall Stover and colleagues)
discovery.note: A bicyclic nitroimidazole described in Nature in 2000; rights passed to the non-profit TB Alliance in 2002.

rx_status: prescription; generic versions prequalified by WHO (Macleods, 2024)
tagline: Nitroimidazole from a non-profit, part of six-month BPaL/BPaLM drug-resistant TB regimens
summary: Pretomanid is a nitroimidazooxazine developed by the non-profit Global Alliance for TB Drug Development (TB Alliance). Approved in 2019 with bedaquiline and linezolid (BPaL) for highly drug-resistant tuberculosis, it enabled all-oral six-month treatment that WHO now recommends for most rifampicin-resistant TB.
mechanism: Pretomanid is a prodrug activated by the mycobacterial deazaflavin (F420)-dependent nitroreductase Ddn. Under aerobic conditions it inhibits mycolic acid biosynthesis, impairing the cell wall of replicating bacilli.

Under hypoxic conditions activation releases reactive nitrogen species, including nitric oxide, that act as respiratory poisons against non-replicating bacteria. Resistance arises from mutations in ddn or in genes of the F420 biosynthesis pathway (fbiA, fbiB, fbiC, fgd1).
uses: Pulmonary extensively drug-resistant, or treatment-intolerant/non-responsive multidrug-resistant tuberculosis, with bedaquiline and linezolid (BPaL)
Rifampicin-resistant TB in the WHO BPaLM regimen (with moxifloxacin)

history.title: Discovery
history.detail: PA-824 is described in Nature by PathoGenesis scientists.

history.title: TB Alliance
history.detail: Chiron (which had acquired PathoGenesis) transfers rights to the TB Alliance.

history.title: Nix-TB results
history.detail: The Nix-TB trial reports about 90% favourable outcomes with BPaL in highly drug-resistant TB.

history.title: US approval
history.detail: The FDA approves pretomanid under the Limited Population Pathway, the third TB drug approved in over 40 years.

history.title: EU approval
history.detail: The European Commission grants a conditional authorisation (Dovprela).

history.title: WHO BPaLM
history.detail: WHO recommends six-month BPaLM (bedaquiline, pretomanid, linezolid, moxifloxacin) for rifampicin-resistant TB.

pk.metabolism: multiple reductive and oxidative pathways (CYP3A4 accounts for about 20%)

common: Peripheral neuropathy and myelosuppression (largely due to linezolid in the regimen)

facts: Pretomanid was the first TB drug developed and registered by a not-for-profit organisation.
The ZeNix trial showed that lower linezolid doses within BPaL reduce toxicity while maintaining efficacy.

references.title: WHO PQ: Macleods pretomanid tablets prequalified
